classification.difficultyReason: Count ordered outcomes without replacement and combine the two possible orders for different colours.

content.prompt: A fishpond has 2 gold fish and 3 black fish. Two fish are taken without replacement, one after another. What is the probability of:

answer.worked:
Distinguish the five fish individually. Without replacement, there are $5\times4=20$ equally likely ordered outcomes. Of these, $2\times1=2$ contain two gold fish.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{two gold fish})&=\frac{2}{20}\\P(\text{two gold fish})&=\frac{1}{10}\end{align*}$$

There are $5\times4=20$ equally likely ordered outcomes. Of these, $3\times2=6$ contain two black fish.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{two black fish})&=\frac{6}{20}\\P(\text{two black fish})&=\frac{3}{10}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: a black and a gold in any order?

answer.worked:
There are $5\times4=20$ equally likely ordered outcomes. Black then gold gives $3\times2=6$ favourable outcomes; gold then black gives $2\times3=6$.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{one of each colour})&=\frac{6+6}{20}\\P(\text{one of each colour})&=\frac{12}{20}\\P(\text{one of each colour})&=\frac{3}{5}\end{align*}$$
